analysis.title: Regime change has been achieved
key_insights: US midterms produced a larger Democratic sweep of the House, Senate and governorships than expected, including a Democratic Senate win in Texas for the first time since 1988 and in South Carolina for the first time since 1998.

Rabobank says the outcome was largely priced in by prediction markets and financial markets. Brent fell more than 10% to $93/bbl, below $100/bbl for the first time since October 7. The S&P 500 rose almost 2% to $7,708.

JD Vance cited a pollster on what converted Trump voters want from the GOP: end the war, focus on cost of living/inflation, put America First, change the GOP relationship with Israel. Vance said the war and high gasoline prices contributed to the GOP loss.
CBS reported that Trump is considering replacing Hegseth, with DeSantis floated as a possible replacement. Trump denied it.
Michael Every says the result raises the chance that Trump backs down over Iran, but a reversal would not necessarily end Middle East hostilities or strengthen the US geostrategically.

Joe DeLaura says leaving Iran dominant in the Persian Gulf would not guarantee flows of oil, aluminium, helium, LNG and fertilizer. Rabobank sees no assurance of sustainably lower oil prices after the initial selloff, which it calls false relief.
Every says Moscow may read the election as reduced US willingness to fight and have less incentive to negotiate with Kyiv, so the Russia-Ukraine war could escalate with energy-market repercussions.

Canada and China extended a trade deal on canola meal, peas, lobster and crab through 2028. Carney says the US is 'asking less' and 'offering more' in trade talks. Rabobank doubts the US has an immediate incentive to ease tariffs on Canada further.

Rabobank's base case is that the Trump Administration will sharpen its focus on Iran in coming weeks, and Marey expects more foreign-policy activity given domestic constraints. Trade deals offer chances for announced 'wins'.

Day ahead: Eurozone September PPI, a Bank of England decision with a 25bp hike to 4.00% unanimously expected by analysts and almost fully priced in OIS, a Banxico decision with a hold at 6.50% expected, the Canadian federal budget, and speeches from Macklem and Rogers, ECB speakers, and Fed speakers Hammack, Barkin and Logan.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A pickup would extend the acceleration in producer prices seen since early 2023.

macro_indicators.reading: In-line print would be the hottest producer price increase since early 2023
macro_indicators.interpretation: Signals renewed producer price pressure in the Eurozone.
Analysts unanimously expect the hike and OIS pricing implies it is almost fully priced in.
Majority of Bloomberg-surveyed analysts and Rabobank expect a hold.
First close below $100/bbl since October 7. Rabobank expects no assured sustained decline.
Equities rallied after the Democratic midterm sweep.

risk_factors: Oil may not fall sustainably, since a US pivot away from Iran does not guarantee Gulf supply flows.
Russia-Ukraine escalation could revive energy-market pressure.
Trump's constrained domestic position may lead to more aggressive foreign-policy activity.
Canada's China trade deal could complicate US market access and tariff relief.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict: midterm result raises the chance Trump backs down, but Rabobank says that would not end Middle East hostilities.
Persian Gulf: Iranian dominance could disrupt flows of oil, aluminium, helium, LNG and fertilizer, and Gulf states could fight a new war or pay for protection.
Russia-Ukraine: Moscow may see less incentive to negotiate and the war could escalate.
US-Canada-China trade: Canada and China extended their trade deal through 2028 while Canada negotiates with the US.
Hegseth replacement reports: CBS says DeSantis is floated as a replacement, Trump denies it.

tension_points.bull_case: A US pivot away from Iran after the election could ease the conflict and lower energy prices, as Brent fell more than 10% to $93/bbl.
tension_points.bear_case: Rabobank says a US pullback offers no assurance of sustainably lower oil prices. Iran could dominate the Gulf and disrupt flows, and a Russia-Ukraine escalation could hit energy markets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Trump backing away from Iran without a durable reopening of Gulf supply flows, or a renewed Russia-Ukraine escalation.

theme_stances.key_argument: A US pivot away from direct involvement offers no assurance of sustainably lower oil prices after the initial selloff of false relief.
Trump's foreign-policy activity is likely to escalate given his constraints at home.
